html:
The Nahua of Michoacán are Nahuatl-speaking communities of the Pacific coast and coastal mountains of Michoacán, Mexico, in towns such as Pómaro, Ostula and Maruata. In 1492 this coast lay at the edge of the Purépecha kingdom, whose heartland was inland around Lake Pátzcuaro.

They are one of the westernmost groups of Nahua people and speak a local form of Nahuatl. They farm, fish and gather on communal land. In 2009 the community of Santa María Ostula took back disputed coastal land and set up its own community guard against cartels and land grabbers, at the cost of many murdered leaders.
